idiom.note: function-based behaviors, stateful_actor for the cached peer, bare uint64_t on the hot path, one handshake outside the window

caveats: CAF's scheduler is a work-stealing pool. 'cores' is a thread BUDGET; the workers are pinned one per CPU via caf::thread_hook so the CPU set matches qb's exactly, but CAF still steals across them, which qb's actors cannot do. That is an architectural difference, and it cuts both ways: stealing costs on a two-actor ping-pong and pays on an unbalanced fan-out

wait=1 raises caf.work-stealing.aggressive-poll-attempts (CAF's spelling of busy-spin) to the profile that measured fastest in docs/TUNING.md; wait=0 leaves CAF's shipped defaults, which on ping-pong are FASTER than any spin profile tried
CAF 1.1.0 builds itself at C++17 -- its own CMake sets the standard -- while qb and the harness are C++20. Forcing CAF to C++20 was not done: it would measure a build CAF does not ship
